newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister hits EU states over mad cow crisis.
newsitem.headline: French minister hits EU states over mad cow crisis.

text.p: French Agriculture Minister Philippe Vasseur accused other European Union nations on Wednesday of mishandling the mad cow crisis and predicted that the hardest part of dealing with the disease was yet to come.
He urged the EU to reform the beef sector in 1997 and said some nations, which he did not name, had been too lax in confronting what he called an "unprecedented crisis."
"The hardest part remains," Vasseur said, referring to EU efforts to revive beef farming and impose strict controls on trade as part of a strategy to eliminate the disease.
"If we've got through part of the crisis it doesn't mean the difficulties have disappeared," he told reporters at a New Year reception.
"I'm not sure that the implications of this crisis have been understood everywhere," he added, refusing to name countries.
Britain triggered the crisis last March by saying that mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), might be transmitted to humans who ate meat from infected cows.

Vasseur said British cows, beef and animal feed had been circulating freely for years in the EU -- meaning it was a threat throughout the 15-nation bloc. France was the first nation to ban imports of British beef, in March.
"We mustn't imagine a "Maginot line' that the prion cannot cross," he said, alluding to the defences France set up between the wars in a bid to prevent an invasion by German troops.
A draft European Parliament report on Monday strongly attacked Britain and the European Commission for mishandling the mad cow crisis but stopped short of demanding specific sanctions.
